title: Hover State
definition: A state variant (`hover:`) that applies a utility class ONLY when the user's mouse cursor is resting over the element.
simpleExplanation: When a user mouses over a blue button, you want it to turn dark blue to signal that it is clickable. You simply add `hover:bg-blue-700`.
realWorldExample: Applying `hover:underline` to a blue text link so it underlines exactly like a classic 1990s webpage when the user puts their mouse over it.

basic: What prefix do you use to change the text color to red when the mouse is over an element?
intermediate: Does the `hover:` state work on mobile touch screens?

answers.question: On mobile?
answers.answer: Mobile phones do not have a mouse cursor. 'Hovering' technically happens for a split second when the user taps the screen with their finger, but it is generally terrible UX to rely on hover states for critical information on mobile devices.
